newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities steady to firmer.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were steady to firmer in quiet late trade as activity was confined to position adjustments ahead of the New Year's Day holiday, dealers said.

Although time decay tends to weigh on option prices before a holiday, especially when underlying markets are as stagnant as they were today, most traders seemed to have finished trading for the year and did not need to sell volatilities, they added.

"Vols have been pretty darn cheap here for quite a while, and I think everybody who wanted to sell volatility going into the holiday has done it," said a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Implied volatilities for CME March and June Eurodollar futures options stood little changed from Friday at 9.0 and 13.6 percent respectively.
In the Treasury bond pit at the Chicago Board of Trade, implied volatilities for February and March T-bond futures options rose 0.1-0.2 point to around 9.3 percent and 9.8 percent.
A brokerage trader at the CBOT said volume was extremely light and there was little to read into it.
"We've got a few 500-lot trades here and there, but nothing really large," he said.
Traders said several U.S. economic figures due out later this week and next week, including the December employment report on January 10, were also underpinning volatilities.

During Tuesday's shortened pre-holiday session, the market will see a pair of weekly retail sales surveys as well as the December Chicago Purchasing Management index, December consumer confidence and November new home sales.
